input.quote: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds. There is no obligation on Vendor to provide transition assistance, and no Customer Data return/export or deletion-certification obligation anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "transition", "machine-readable", "delet" and "return" surface only the passing reference to "any agreed transition period" in 10.1 (which presupposes an agreement that does not exist) and Section 16.5, which expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in the document and Section 15 contains no return or deletion duty. In a hosted-services agreement this absence is a deviation under the playbook, so we insert a new Section 10.3 with the model language: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export).

ops.text: 10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10 ends access and settles Deliverables and refunds but gives us no exit help or route to recover Customer Data, and Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to a Section 11 that does not exist in this Agreement. We have added our standard exit clause: up to six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter; if six months is difficult we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.
proposal.summary: Insert new Section 10.3 requiring up to 6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.
